question.text: For a diatomic ideal gas in a closed system, which of the following plots does not correctly describe the relation between various thermodynamic quantities?

solution.text:
Cp is molar heat capacity at constant pressure. Since the quantity is defined at constant pressure, it does not vary with pressure.
At higher temperatures, the rotational degree of freedom becomes active.
$C_P=\frac{7}{2} R \quad \text { (Independent of } P \text { ) }$
$\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{V}}=\frac{5}{2} \mathrm{R} \quad \text { (Independent of } \mathrm{V} \text { ) }$
$\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{V}}$ depends on $\mathrm{T}$ and independent on $\mathrm{V}$.
$\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{P}}$ depends on $\mathrm{T}$ and independent on $\mathrm{P}$.
